sun.upright:
Aries Suns tend to take a thing on because someone said it couldn't be done, or because doing it yourself is quicker than explaining it to anyone else. That's how most of the staves in this bundle got collected, one at a time, each one a small dare accepted. The card is Saturn in Sagittarius, and Sagittarius is fire like you, four signs away in a trine, so every new commitment feels like your kind of thing and slides on with no friction at all.

The difficulty is Saturn. It's the planet that normally says hang on, what's this going to cost, and in Aries it's in fall, which means it's badly placed and struggles to be heard. You don't get the early warning other people get. You find out how heavy the load is once you're already carrying it, and by then putting any of it down feels like losing, which an Aries Sun takes personally. The Emperor, your sign's Major, is a man who runs everything himself. I'd guess you've been doing a fair impression of him lately, and it's wearing you out more than you're letting anyone see.

At work it's the project you volunteered for before the meeting had finished, plus the two you picked up because a colleague was slow. In the body it's training through a sore knee because a rest day feels like going backwards. With a partner it's saying you've got it when they offer to help, and meaning it kindly. Pick the one you took on to prove a point, and hand it back to whoever it really belongs to.
sun.reversed:
Upside down, this card on an Aries Sun usually means you've gone faster to stay ahead of the pile. More yeses, shorter nights, less patience, and a quiet fury at anyone who suggests slowing down. Mars rules Aries and doesn't know how to retreat, and with Saturn in fall there's nothing in you that can make it. So the load keeps growing, and the fire that normally makes you good company comes out as a short fuse.

It shows at work as the job you won't admit you can't finish, done at midnight and done worse than you'd like. At the gym, or on the bike, it's an injury you keep pushing through. And at home somebody's getting snapped at for asking a simple question. Put the whole lot on the table in front of you, on paper if you have to, and pick up again only what has your name on it.

moon.upright:
Feelings don't sit still in an Aries Moon. Something upsets you and you want to do something about it straight away, fix it, argue it, go for a run, and once it's out of your system you're usually fine. The Ten of Wands, drawn for your tides, suggests the doing has got ahead of the feeling. Every restless mood has turned into another job, and the jobs have piled up.

Sagittarius and Aries are both fire, in an easy trine, so this happens without you noticing. Taking something on feels better than sitting with a bad mood, and it's quicker too. Saturn, the planet behind this card, is in fall in Aries, which means the part of you that would say stop, you're tired, can't get a word in. A Mars Moon would honestly rather be exhausted than idle. You probably know what it's like to lie on the couch on a Sunday afternoon, feel worse instead of better, and get up to clean the car. The busyness is keeping something at arm's length, and it might be worth finding out what.

Sleep is the first thing to go, cut short so you can get more done. The temper comes next, usually aimed at whoever's closest when one more thing lands. With your body it's the workout that was meant to calm you down and has turned into another thing to win. Next time a feeling comes up, give it ten minutes before you act on it. Sit down, put the phone somewhere else and let it be there.
moon.reversed:
When the card turns over on an Aries Moon, the fire has nowhere left to go. You've taken on so much that there isn't even room to do the usual thing and burn a mood off, so it stays in you and gets hotter. Anger comes fast, over very small things. Then comes guilt, and then, because that's how a Mars Moon copes, another task to make up for it.

It tends to show at home first, with the people least able to get out of the way. Sleep goes thin and jumpy, and your body carries it as a tight chest or a jaw you notice clenched at the traffic lights. The easy trine with Sagittarius makes all of it feel normal, which is half the trouble. Before you pick up anything new, cancel one thing outright, then go for a slow walk with nowhere to be.

rising.upright:
Aries rising comes through the door already moving, and strangers read that as someone who'll handle it. Whatever it is. So they hand it to you, and you take it, and that's how the load in this card builds up on your Ascendant. Mars rules your chart, which makes for a quick first impression with a bit of challenge in it. Sagittarius is fire too, trine to Aries, so each new thing you're handed feels natural to accept.

What makes this card harder for you is Saturn. It's in fall in Aries, and in plain terms that means patience and pacing don't come easily to the way you start things. You're wonderful in the first week of anything. The long middle, the part where ten staves have to be carried all the way to town, is where you flag, and people who met you at full speed can't see why. There's a gap between how much you look like you can take on and how much you've actually got left, and you're the only one who knows about it.

In a new job it's being given the difficult client in your first month, because you said yes so fast in the interview. With a new group of friends it's becoming the one who books the table and organises the weekend away, every time. On a first date it's offering to help with their move. Let someone else go first in the next meeting, and say nothing about what you could take on until you've heard what they need.
rising.reversed:
This card reversed makes Aries rising look stretched to strangers. You arrive late, or flustered, or too quick with an answer, and the speed that usually reads as confidence reads as a person with far too much on. Or you over-promise in the first ten minutes to seem capable, and spend the next month paying for it. Mars rules your Ascendant and hates to be seen struggling, so you cover it with more speed.

New colleagues may have worked out you're overloaded before you've admitted it. In a first meeting with anyone, the temper can show at something small, a slow waiter, a late train, and it leaves the wrong impression. With a partner's friends it's volunteering to drive everyone home and then being short with them in the car. Get to the next thing five minutes early, sit down, and let the other person do the offering.

sun.upright:
There's a particular kind of tired that comes from carrying something you chose years ago and can't bring yourself to put down, and a Taurus Sun knows it well. You picked these things carefully. You've put years into them. Dropping one now would feel like wasting everything that went in. Sagittarius, the card's sign, is five signs from yours, a quincunx, an angle where two signs share nothing and have to keep adjusting. Fire and earth don't naturally help each other either, so the card's restless take-on-more energy has never suited your pace, and you've been carrying its extras at your own steady speed.

There's one link worth knowing. Saturn rules the last ten degrees of Taurus, the Seven of Pentacles, a card of a man leaning on his hoe and looking at what he's grown. That's the question for your Sun. You're very good at keeping going. You're much less good at stopping to check which of these plants still deserve watering. Venus rules Taurus and likes things that last, and I've seen plenty of Taurus Suns keep a job, a committee or a friendship going for years after it stopped giving them anything, because letting it go would mean admitting it wasn't forever.

At work it's the role you've quietly outgrown and still do perfectly. With money it's the extra hours that were meant to be temporary and are now part of the budget. At home it's a renovation or a garden that's become a chore. Pick the one thing you'd stop tending if nobody would mind, and tell the person it affects.
sun.reversed:
The reversed Ten on a Taurus Sun is stubbornness doing the carrying. You know the load's too heavy. You've known for a while. But you've decided, and a fixed earth sign that has decided doesn't like being told, even by its own back. So the pile stays exactly where it is and you just go slower under it.

At work it looks like a backlog you defend instead of clearing, with a flat no for anyone who offers to take part of it. With money it's paying for things you no longer use because cancelling them feels like a loss. The body gets the bill, usually in the neck and jaw, with a tiredness that sleep doesn't touch. Choose the least useful thing you're holding onto and end it properly, with an email or a phone call, then notice how quickly you stop missing it.

moon.upright:
Once something becomes part of the routine, a Taurus Moon stops noticing its weight. That's the weak spot in a system that otherwise works beautifully for you. The same breakfast, the same chair, the same walk, people who stay put. It's how you feel safe. But the school run, a parent's shopping, the friend who rings every night to talk things through, each of them got added to the routine and none of them ever came off.

Fire and earth have no natural bond, so the card's energy doesn't sit easily with your Moon. The Sagittarius side keeps adding, and the Taurus side keeps absorbing, quietly and without fuss, because making a fuss isn't your way. Saturn has no real standing in Taurus and picks up the colour of Venus, your Moon's ruler, so the load often looks like comfort you're giving other people, the dinners, the lifts, the listening. That's why it's so hard to put down. It feels like love, and mostly it is. It's also heavy, and your body knows before you do, usually as a sore lower back or a tiredness that seems to be in your bones.

At home you might be the one who holds all the small arrangements, and nobody else knows where anything is kept. Sleep goes deep and still doesn't refresh you. With a partner there may be something you haven't said about who does what. Take one job off your routine, a real one, and let someone else do it their way, even if their way is worse.
moon.reversed:
Turned over, this card on a Taurus Moon usually means you've gone quiet under the load. You keep doing everything, the cooking, the remembering, the steady presence, and you've stopped enjoying any of it, and you don't say a word. Taurus can take a great deal before it complains. Then one day it doesn't complain, it just withdraws, and the people around you have no idea what happened.

It shows in the body as heaviness, as comfort eating or no appetite at all, and sleep that doesn't help. At home it can be a sulk that lasts days. Venus rules your Moon, and it needs a bit of pleasure that doesn't have to be earned. Have one thing that's only for you, a bath, a nap, a long lunch on your own, and don't do a single job first to deserve it.

rising.upright:
People meet a Taurus rising and relax. You look unhurried and unbothered, someone who won't be rattled, and that's exactly why this card matters on your Ascendant. You look as if you've got room for more. So more arrives. Venus rules your chart and gives you a calm, pleasant face, and people take that face as capacity.

Sagittarius and Taurus are five signs apart, the quincunx, an angle of constant small adjustment, and fire laid over your earth never quite settles. You'll feel it as a gap between the way you seem and what you're actually holding. Taurus rising also doesn't like to refuse, because refusing would disturb the calm, and the calm is what people like about you. So you take the extra thing without changing expression, and then the next. Someone who's only just met you has no idea you're at the limit, because nothing on your face has moved. That's the most common Taurus rising story with this card, in my experience, and it tends to run until something physical stops it.

In a new job it's being the steady one in the second week and the buried one by the third month. With neighbours it's the parcels, the key-minding, the dog on weekends. On a date it's being the easy-going one who goes along with every plan. The next time someone asks for something you don't have room for, let your face show it, and say it's a bad week.
rising.reversed:
With the Ten reversed, Taurus rising can dig in behind its calm. You go on looking fine long after you've stopped coping, and the steadier you look, the less anyone thinks to check. Or the stubbornness shows through. You come across as immovable, turning down help in a way that reads as pride, and some people take it personally.

It shows in a new workplace, where you're handed the extra project because you never flinch. It shows with friends, who assume you're sorted and stop offering. On a first date it can look like there's not much going on, when there's actually too much. Venus rules your chart and wants everything to look pleasant, your troubles included. Tell one person the real size of your week, in plain words and without turning it into a joke.

sun.upright:
Sagittarius is Gemini's opposite sign, the far end of the same line across the zodiac, so this card is looking at you from directly across the room. Gemini gathers lots of small things, the ideas, the people, the side projects, three books on the go at once. Sagittarius wants one big thing that means something. The Ten of Wands is what it looks like when the many small things have become a load, and none of them adds up to the one big thing.

Air feeds fire, so everything catches easily with you. Someone mentions an idea and you're in. A friend needs help and you're halfway through a plan before they've finished the sentence. Saturn has no real standing in Gemini and takes on Mercury's colour here, so it doesn't stop any of it. It just keeps count, quietly, and the count is high. The Lovers is your sign's Major, and it's a card about choosing, which is what's missing. You haven't had to choose, because Mercury can keep a lot of plates spinning, and it's only lately that the plates have got too heavy.

At work it's having a finger in every project and being the go-to person for all of them, with nothing properly finished. In friendships it's the plans made with real enthusiasm and cancelled the day before. On your phone it's the forty open tabs. Write every commitment on one sheet of paper, cross out half, and tell the people concerned before the day is out.
sun.reversed:
Reversed on a Gemini Sun, the Ten of Wands tends to look like a lot of beginnings. You keep starting because starting is the fun part, and you keep not finishing because by then something new has turned up. From outside it looks like energy. From inside it feels more and more like failing, and Mercury, your ruler, is very good at telling you so at two in the morning.

At work it shows as a reputation for bright ideas and a quiet worry about delivery. With friends it's the messages left unanswered, because answering all of them feels impossible, so you answer none. The opposite pull from Sagittarius, toward one thing that matters, only makes the scatter feel worse. Pick the smallest unfinished thing you have and finish it completely before you start anything else.

moon.upright:
It's the mental list that does it. Who needs a lift on Thursday, whose birthday it is, which friend isn't speaking to which, the appointment, the form, the reply you still owe. A Gemini Moon calms down by talking, texting, reading up, finding out, and it processes a feeling by putting it into words, usually with someone. So the load in this card is mostly in your head.

Sagittarius sits opposite Gemini, and there's a pull in that between the dozens of small facts you're holding and some larger sense of what it's all for, which you can't quite reach under everything else. Fire and air feed each other, so your mind catches easily and won't switch off. One thought lights the next. Saturn, taking on Mercury's colour in your sign, turns every one of those facts into an obligation. A Gemini Moon carrying everyone's details can feel it's being useful while quietly running itself into the ground, and I see it often. The worry is rarely loud, it just runs all day in the background, and you've stopped noticing it.

It shows at night, with your phone on the pillow and your mind still going. It shows in the family group chat, where you're the one who keeps track of everything. It might show with a sibling who's leaning on you for more than you've got. Get the list out of your head and onto paper, then give some of it away to someone who can remember it just as well.
moon.reversed:
When this card reverses on a Gemini Moon, the talking stops helping. You go over the worry in your own head, again and again, until the going over is the worry. Fire and air feed each other the wrong way here, one anxious thought catching on the next. You might be scrolling for relief and getting none, or chatting brightly to people while feeling like static inside.

Sleep is where it shows first, then a short temper with whoever asks for one more thing. With a friend or a sibling you might have gone quiet in a way that isn't like you. Mercury rules your Moon and needs someone to talk to, and lately it's only been talking to itself. Say the worry out loud to one person, in a single conversation, and let them hold some of it.

rising.upright:
In a good conversation, Gemini rising will agree to almost anything, and that's the doorway this card comes through. Quick, funny, curious, you ask good questions and people come away feeling they've known you for years. So they ask things of you almost at once, you say yes in the flow of it, and the Ten of Wands is what the diary looks like a month later. Mercury rules your chart, and a Mercury Ascendant tends to agree first and sort out the details afterwards.

Your rising sign sits opposite the card's Sagittarius, so the way you meet people is being pulled toward its opposite, toward depth and follow-through, which is the part that carries weight. Fire and air get on easily. Things catch. Saturn has no grip in Gemini, so there's nothing to brake the yes. You seem light, and mostly you are, and nobody imagines the light one is carrying anything heavy. People keep handing you one more thing because you took the last one so cheerfully.

At work it's becoming the coordinator of a project you only asked a question about. With new friends it's the group chat you started and now run. At a party it's promising three people three different favours before the night's over. The next time someone asks you for something, say you'll let them know tomorrow, and use the evening to decide.
rising.reversed:
The reversed Ten makes Gemini rising say yes, regret it, and then say yes again to cover the first one. You agree in the moment because the conversation's nice, and later you're overpromised to people you barely know, with a low guilt that has you avoiding them in the supermarket. Or you over-explain every no until you've talked yourself back into it.

It shows in a calendar you dread opening, and with new colleagues who've noticed the gap between the offer and the delivery. On a date it can look like being great fun and then vanishing for a week. Mercury rules your chart and loves a quick answer. Keep your next no short, one sentence and no reasons, and then change the subject.

sun.upright:
Most of what's in this bundle, for a Cancer Sun, is other people. You build your sense of who you are around looking after them, and you're good at it, and the looking after is usually what's become too heavy. Saturn is in detriment in Cancer, opposite Capricorn, the sign it rules. In practice that means Saturn's gift for limits and structure works against the grain in your sign, and you can feel the effort of it. Saying no to someone you love is the hardest work a Cancer Sun does.

Then there are the elements. The card is fire and you're water, which makes steam, or one putting the other out. You'll recognise the steam. It's the resentment that builds while you keep caring, the sharp tone that comes out of nowhere and surprises you as much as anyone. Your sign's Major is The Chariot, a driver in armour going forward, and with this card the armour has turned into something you carry for everyone else. You probably took on each piece for a good reason. Together they're too much, and I'd guess you've known that for a while without saying it.

At home it's being the one who keeps the family running, the appointments, the meals, the phone calls. With an ageing parent it may be doing more than your siblings and keeping quiet about the difference. At work you're the one the team comes to when things go wrong. Let someone you love struggle a little with something this week without stepping in, and watch them manage.
sun.reversed:
Reversed, the Ten of Wands on a Cancer Sun is caring that's gone sour. You keep doing everything because nobody else will, or so you've decided, and you keep a running tally of what goes unthanked. Then the tally comes out, at the wrong moment, and the people you've been looking after are hurt and confused. With Saturn in detriment in your sign, the caring has no shape to it, so it spreads to fill every hour you've got.

At home it shows as doing it all and seething. At work it's covering for a colleague and then crying in the car. Tell one person plainly that you're carrying too much, name the exact piece you need them to take, and let them take it, even if they do it differently from you.

moon.upright:
The Moon rules Cancer, so a Cancer Moon feels things at full strength and remembers them for years. The birthday someone forgot, a kindness from a stranger in 2009, the exact tone in the kitchen last Tuesday. This card says those feelings have turned into something you're carrying, other people's as much as your own. A Cancer Moon picks up the mood of a room the way a sponge picks up water, and it doesn't wring itself out.

Saturn's in detriment in Cancer, which matters for this card, because Saturn is the planet that sets limits and in your sign it can't do that job comfortably. It keeps trying to organise feelings that were only ever meant to be felt. You'll know the result. You manage everyone's emotions, checking in, smoothing things over, keeping track of who's upset with whom, and at the end of the day there's nothing left for your own. The card's fire against your water makes a low simmer underneath all of it, a crossness you don't quite admit to.

Your stomach usually knows first, with a knot or a loss of appetite. Sleep follows, broken by thinking about someone else's problem. With your mother, or whoever raised you, there may be an old job you still do for them without being asked. Tell one person, kindly, that there's something of theirs you've been holding, and give it back.
moon.reversed:
Flipped over, the card can leave a Cancer Moon drowning in feelings, most of them not yours to begin with. Old hurts come back all at once, and the harder you try to get a grip on them the worse it gets, because a Cancer Moon can't be told out of a mood. It has to be looked after out of one. You're mothering everyone except yourself.

It shows as lying awake at three going over a conversation. It shows in eating, too much or not at all, and a stomach that's in knots. At home you might retreat into your shell and then feel hurt that nobody came after you. Do something small and warm for your body first, a hot drink, a blanket, a bath, and then ring one person you can be honest with.

rising.upright:
Cancer rising meets the world a bit sideways. You check whether a place is safe before you open up, and once you have, you look after people completely. That looking after is how this card gets in. You start most things by taking care of someone, the new colleague, the nervous guest, the friend of a friend at the party, and that's how the load gets strapped on.

Sagittarius and Cancer are a quincunx apart, five signs, with almost nothing in common, so the card's energy never quite fits the way you meet the world and there's a constant small adjustment going on. The Moon rules your chart, and your face shows your mood more than you'd like. With this card, people are likely to see you as steady and caring, and they lean. They don't see the effort underneath, because Cancer rising keeps its softest parts inside the shell. I've known a lot of people with this Ascendant who become everyone's confidant within a week of starting a job, and after a year nobody knows a thing about them.

At work it's becoming the team's glue before anyone's learnt your surname. In a friendship group it's being the one who notices who's gone quiet and checks on them. With a partner's family it's helping in the kitchen until you're the one doing all the washing up. Let someone look after you early, before you've done anything for them, and just say thank you.
rising.reversed:
The reversed card can close Cancer rising's shell right up. You keep the caring face on and feel completely alone behind it, and because you look like you need nothing, nobody offers. Fire and water in this pairing make steam, and here it's the kind that builds with the lid on.

It shows at work as being everyone's confidant and nobody's concern. With friends it's a hurt that you've looked after them for years and they haven't noticed you're struggling. It can come out as snapping at a stranger, a waiter or someone on the phone, which isn't like you at all. Let one person see you're having a hard time before they have to guess, and let them help with one practical thing.

sun.upright:
Leo Suns like to be the one who can. The friend who hosts, the colleague who saves the pitch, the parent at every game, the person everyone says they couldn't do without. It's a warm way to live, and the Ten of Wands shows where it leads when you keep saying yes to stay that person. Sagittarius and Leo are both fire, a trine, so taking on more feels generous and natural. Same element turns the volume up, on the good and on the too much.

Saturn is the difficulty. It's in detriment in Leo, opposite Aquarius, one of the signs it rules, so its sense for limits works against your grain and doesn't get much of a hearing. It does have one foothold in your sign. Saturn rules the first ten degrees of Leo, the Five of Wands, a card about everyone competing at once, and I think that's part of what's going on. You don't want to be the one who drops out. You took most of this on to be seen as big-hearted and capable, and you are both. The pride that picked up the load is also what won't let you put any of it down, because dropping something feels like letting the audience down, and Leo hates that.

At work it's being the hero of the deadline, staying late so the team can go home, and being quietly hurt when they do. With friends it's the hosting, the organising, the picking up of the bill. With children it's being at every event and never getting a quiet Sunday. Let one visible thing go undone, the party or the favour, and notice who still turns up.
sun.reversed:
Upturned, the Ten on a Leo Sun is pride holding the load up. You're sinking and you won't say so, because the image matters, and the more tired you get the brighter you smile. Saturn in detriment can't make you count the cost, and the trine with Sagittarius keeps the fire roaring well past sense.

It shows at work as a brittle cheerfulness and a flash of temper when someone asks how you're managing it all. With friends you keep hosting and paying and organising, furious underneath that nobody offers anything back. Your body might feel it in the back or the chest, a heaviness you ignore. Tell one person who's earned it that you're not okay, and let them see it on your face.

moon.upright:
Big birthday plans, the gift someone mentioned once in passing, the meal made from scratch, the dramatic rescue when a friend's in trouble. That's how a Leo Moon shows love, with both hands, and it needs the warmth to come back. Here the Ten of Wands says the giving has turned into a job, and you're tired from it, and a bit hurt that nobody's noticed.

Leo and the card's Sagittarius are both fire, in a trine, so your generosity flows without a brake. Saturn, in detriment in Leo, is the planet that ought to say that's enough now, and it can barely make itself heard. So you keep going. What you'll recognise is the sulk. You've done all this, and someone forgot to say thank you, and now you're wounded in a way that's out of proportion, and you know it's out of proportion, and that makes it worse. A Leo Moon that only gives and never gets to receive ends up hungry, and it can be a long while before it admits it.

At home it's being the one who makes every occasion special, then collapsing afterwards. With friends it's the ones you give most to who seem to take you for granted. In the body it's a tiredness around the chest and upper back. When someone next offers you something, a compliment, a lift, a favour, just take it, and don't pay it back straight away.
moon.reversed:
Reversed, the card on a Leo Moon turns warmth into wounded pride. You've given a lot and felt unseen, and the hurt pushes you to give even more, as if a big enough gesture will finally get the reaction you need. Or you go the other way and withdraw dramatically, waiting to be noticed, which never works as well as you hope.

It shows as sulking you won't name and a mental list of every unthanked kindness. You might notice you're keeping score, and hating that you are. At home it can be a partner who feels they can't do anything right. The Sun rules Leo and needs warmth coming in as well as going out. Stop giving extra for a week, the favours and the effort, and see who comes toward you anyway.

rising.upright:
Leo rising fills a doorway. People notice you first, the laugh, the hair, the ease, and they tend to decide straight away that you're the one in charge. This card is about what comes with that. When you look confident people hand you things, and a Leo Ascendant doesn't like to look as though anything's too much. The Sun rules your chart, and it wants to be seen at full strength.

Sagittarius and Leo are both fire, a trine, and the yes comes easily and grandly. The card's weight follows. Saturn is in detriment in Leo, which in plain terms means pacing yourself doesn't come naturally to your first move. You make an entrance, you make an offer, and then you have to live up to it. The man on this card is bent right over, and he can't even see the town he's walking to. That's what's behind the big confident start for you, and you'd hate for anyone to notice. So you keep the performance going while your arms shake.

In your first week somewhere new you run the room, and by the fifth you're quietly drowning. At a party it's promising to host the next one. With a new partner it's planning every date yourself. Walk into the next room without needing to run it, and notice that people still like you.
rising.reversed:
Upside down on Leo rising, the card makes coping into a show. You perform being fine so well that everyone believes it, and the confident look keeps drawing more onto shoulders that are already giving way. Or the effort shows through, and you come across as grand and a bit stretched, bright in the voice and tired around the eyes.

It shows at work, where the applause keeps the extra projects coming. Socially you're admired and not much helped, because you've made needing anything look impossible. With family it can be organising every gathering and then leaving early, worn out. The Sun rules your chart and warmth is its best feature, which gets lost when you're performing. Next time someone asks how you are, give them the true answer, and keep it short.

sun.upright:
One small correction at a time, a Virgo Sun can end up carrying the whole office. You like being useful, and more than that, you like being the one who gets it right. You notice the mistake on page forty and you fix it quietly. This card is what happens when being useful and getting it right turn into being buried.

Sagittarius squares Virgo. Both are mutable signs, three apart, and a square is friction that forces your hand. The card's Sagittarius side wants to take on more and see the big picture, your Virgo side wants to do one thing properly, and the rub between them keeps generating work. Every job you take on turns out to have ten smaller jobs inside it. Saturn has no special standing in Virgo and takes on Mercury's colour here, so it brings the weight and a very busy mind, with not much sense of when to stop. The Hermit belongs to Virgo, a man on his own with a lantern, and you might recognise the wish to be left alone to get on with it. I'd guess you're also redoing what other people have rushed, because it's quicker than explaining, and resenting it a little.

At work it's checking everyone's work in the day and doing your own at night. With your health it's a stomach that knots and a list that keeps running after you've lain down. At home it's re-stacking the dishwasher after someone else has loaded it. Let one thing go out good enough this week, and leave it alone afterwards.
sun.reversed:
This card reversed on a Virgo Sun is standards that won't let anything be finished. You polish and correct and catch everyone else's mistakes, because a flaw left standing nags at you, and the square with Sagittarius keeps throwing up more to fix. Saturn has no grip in your sign to tell you when enough is enough.

It shows as a pile of things almost done, and in the people at home, who've started to feel watched. The body tends to carry it in the gut. At work you might be quietly doing someone else's job and then feeling invisible. Mercury rules Virgo and never runs out of things to notice. Hand the next task back at eighty percent, and don't touch it when it comes back imperfect.

moon.upright:
When you're upset, you clean. You make a list, you sort out somebody's problem, and the doing calms you down. That's how a Virgo Moon settles, and it's usually a good system. The Ten of Wands says it's got out of hand. The sorting has become a treadmill, and every problem you fix seems to bring two more along with it.

Fire and earth are neutral to each other, so the card's energy doesn't warm your Moon. It only adds weight. The square between Sagittarius and Virgo is friction that keeps producing more to do. What you'll recognise is worry dressed up as being helpful. You take on the managing of everyone's details, the forms, the appointments, the meal plans, because leaving them undone feels unbearable, and the managing never quite quiets the worry. If anything it feeds it. Mercury rules your Moon and always has one more thing to check. Most Virgo Moons I've known can't rest until the list is done, and they keep adding to it.

Your stomach tends to react to stress before your head admits there is any. Sleep gets lost to tomorrow's list. With a partner there might be a running commentary on how they fold the towels, and you know perfectly well it isn't about the towels. Leave one small thing undone on purpose, a drawer or an email, and let a day go by without fixing it.
moon.reversed:
Under the reversed Ten, a Virgo Moon's worry stops being useful and just runs. Every undone thing becomes proof that something's wrong, and the tidying that used to soothe you now only shows how much more there is. You may be managing everyone's details to quiet a dread that won't be quieted. The square with Sagittarius produces something new to be anxious about as soon as you clear the old one.

It shows in a churning stomach, broken sleep, and a voice in your head that criticises everything, including how you're coping. At home, small things set you off. Get out of your head and into your body, a walk, a proper meal you actually taste, and leave one thing unfixed on purpose until tomorrow.

rising.upright:
Whatever's broken in a room tends to find its way to a Virgo rising. You come across as tidy, observant and quietly capable, the sort of person who'll spot what's wrong and probably fix it. That's the first thing to know about this card on your Ascendant. You meet the world by noticing what needs doing, and that's a magnet for other people's undone jobs.

Your rising sign squares the card's Sagittarius, both mutable signs, and the friction there keeps producing more. The elements don't help. Earth and fire are strangers to each other, so none of it warms you, it's just work. Mercury, your chart ruler, keeps you half listening for the problem in every conversation. You look sorted, and nobody imagines the sorted person could use a hand. You probably don't ask either, because asking would feel like admitting the tidy front is only a front. I've seen Virgo risings take on the admin of an entire office within a month of starting, without anyone ever asking them to.

Starting a new job, you're the fixer in the first fortnight and the dumping ground by the second month. With a new friend it's helping with their CV or their tax return over the second coffee. In a shared house it's being the only one who knows which night the bins go out. When you see a problem, let it sit for a day and watch whether someone else picks it up.
rising.reversed:
The reversed Ten turns Virgo rising's competence into a trap. You come across as so on top of every detail that work flows to you and offers of help never do. Or the strain leaks out as nit-picking, correcting a small fact or straightening a pile of papers, and people read it as judgement when it's actually overload.

At work it shows as being indispensable and running on empty. With a partner's friends it's being polite and hard to reach. On a first date it can come across as an inspection. The square with Sagittarius means whatever lands on you tends to land slightly wrong. Tell your manager, or whoever hands out the work, that you're at capacity, in one sentence, before they give you the next thing.

sun.upright:
Libra Suns hate leaving anyone out. You see both sides, you keep things pleasant, and you're usually the one making sure the arrangement is fair. With this card, fair has tipped into you carrying more than your share so that nobody else is put out. A lot of what's on your back belongs to other people, taken on because saying no felt unkind or would have caused a fuss.

The good news is in the astrology. Saturn is exalted in Libra, which means it's an honoured guest in your sign and shows itself at its most principled. Of all the signs, yours is one of the best placed to use what this card is teaching, which is that fairness has to include you. Sagittarius sits sextile to Libra, two signs apart, a helpful angle that still needs you to make a move, and your air fans the card's fire, so agreements come quickly. That's partly how you got here. Saturn also rules the middle ten degrees of Libra, the Three of Swords, and to be honest, the hurt in that card is often what happens when a Libra finally notices how uneven things have got.

At work it's mediating everyone's disagreements and ending up doing two jobs. In a relationship it's keeping score quietly while telling your partner it's fine. With friends it's always being the one who organises the group booking and fronts the money for it. Draw one line this week, fairly and politely, and hold it when someone doesn't love it.
sun.reversed:
Libra Suns with this card reversed tend to carry things just to keep the peace. You said yes again, the pile is mostly other people's, and you can't see how to hand it back without a scene. So you keep the surface gracious and seethe underneath. Saturn is exalted in your sign, which means the fair line you need is well within reach. It's the thought of someone's disappointed face that stops you.

It shows as a diary packed with favours and a resentment that leaks out sideways, a sharp comment at dinner, a late reply. In a partnership it can be the chores, the money and the planning, all quietly yours. At work you might be sorting out a conflict that isn't yours. Say one clear no, once, and apologise for no more than a sentence.

moon.upright:
You notice tension the second you walk into a room, and some part of you starts working on it before you've taken your coat off. That's a Libra Moon. You feel safest when everyone's getting along. The Ten of Wands points straight at it. Keeping the peace has become the weight, and you've been holding the mood for everyone.

Saturn is exalted in Libra, which is unusual and useful. It means the card's hard lesson about fair limits has a good chance of landing with you, better than it would with most signs. The sextile to Sagittarius and the easy meeting of fire and air make it simple to say yes to smoothing things over, and that's how the load crept up. You absorb other people's tension so the room stays calm. It feels like care, and it is, and it also empties you slowly, because the peace you're making costs you your own say. Venus rules Libra and wants everyone happy, and you've been counting yourself last.

It shows when you agree to plans you don't want so there's no awkwardness. It shows in your shoulders, which go up whenever voices do. In your family it might be the go-between role you've had since you were small. Let one small disagreement stand without smoothing it, and notice that everyone's still speaking to each other the next day.
moon.reversed:
Turned over on a Libra Moon, the Ten becomes peace kept at your own expense. You swallow every objection so there's no ripple, and the swallowed feelings turn into anxiety and a resentment you'd never say out loud. Saturn is well placed in your sign, so the fair-mindedness you need is there. It's the fear of conflict that keeps talking you out of it.

It shows as indecision that's really a fear of disappointing someone, and as sleep broken by things you didn't say. With a partner it might be agreeing to everything and then feeling oddly flat. Venus rules your Moon and likes things lovely, and lately only you have been paying for that. Say one small preference out loud, where to eat or what to watch, and stick with it when someone pushes back a little.

rising.upright:
Accommodating people get handed a lot, and Libra rising is very accommodating. You meet people with charm and a real knack for making them comfortable, so you come across as gracious and easy, and that's where the trouble starts with this card. With Venus ruling your chart, you'd sooner do the extra thing yourself than watch someone's face fall.

Your rising sign is sextile to the card's Sagittarius, an easy opening, and fire and air get on, so you agree readily and the load builds fast. The saving grace is Saturn. It's exalted in Libra, which means a fair, well-set limit actually suits the way you present, once you let yourself use it. People respect a Libra rising who says no nicely far more than you'd expect. Underneath the pleasant front, though, there's a resentment growing at how one-sided things have become. I think you've noticed it. You just haven't known how to change it without looking unpleasant.

With new people you become the accommodating one straight away, and the taken-for-granted one soon after. At work you smooth over every bit of friction until the smoothing is a second job. On a date it's going along with the restaurant, the film and the plan for next weekend. Next time you're asked for something, let a short silence sit before you answer, and let one person be a little disappointed in you.
rising.reversed:
With this card upside down, Libra rising's charm can turn into a mask that never comes off. You please everyone and you're honest with no one, and the pleasantness keeps drawing more your way while hiding how stretched you are. Somewhere along the line your own wants dropped out of it. Saturn is exalted in your rising sign, so the fair limit you need is already part of your nature. You just haven't used it in a while.

At work you're everyone's favourite and privately overloaded. In a friendship group your plans are always built around everyone else's. On dates it can look like having no opinion at all. Disappoint one person on purpose, over something small, and notice that it passes.

sun.upright:
Every stave in this bundle, for a Scorpio Sun, is something you didn't trust anyone else to hold. You don't do anything by halves. You commit completely or not at all, and when something matters to you, you'd much prefer to carry it yourself than hand it to someone who might drop it. That's the root of the load in this card for you.

Scorpio and Sagittarius are neighbours on the wheel, a semi-sextile, with little in common and each holding what the other lacks. So the card's outward, restless energy sits a bit oddly on your fixed depth. Fire and water are opposed as elements, and the friction there is steam, a pressure that builds and doesn't vent. Saturn has no special standing in Scorpio and takes on the colour of Mars, your traditional ruler, which gives it an edge of grim determination. You'll push through. You always do. Death is your sign's Major, and it's a card about letting something finish so the next thing can start. I'd guess there's at least one thing in the pile that's already over, and you're still carrying it out of loyalty or pride.

At work it's refusing to delegate, because handing something over means losing control of it. In love it's carrying the relationship's hard parts on your own and not telling your partner you're doing it. The body keeps it in the jaw, and in sleep that never goes deep enough. Hand one real task to someone this week and let them do it their way, without checking.
sun.reversed:
Turned the other way, the card on a Scorpio Sun usually means control has won out over exhaustion. You'd sooner do the work of three than trust anyone to share it, and you clutch every task and every secret. Saturn gives no relief in your sign, only more pressure. The card's fire boils against your water, and the steam has nowhere to go, so it comes out cold instead of loud.

It shows as a tight body and a resentment you feed in private. At work it can look like hoarding information so nobody else can do your job. With a partner it's the silence that means you're angry and won't say why. Choose someone who's earned it, hand them one thing completely, and don't check on it for a week.

moon.upright:
Nobody else can see what a Scorpio Moon is carrying, and that's usually by design. You feel things deeply and privately, you need to trust someone completely before you let them in, and once you've been hurt you don't forget it. So when the Ten of Wands comes up for your Moon, the load is mostly emotional and mostly invisible.

Saturn has no footing in Scorpio, so it brings pressure without relief. The card's fire meets your deep water and turns to steam, heat building under a very still surface. Scorpio and Sagittarius are only neighbours, a semi-sextile, sharing very little, so the weight doesn't sit naturally with how you'd usually hold things. What you'll recognise is carrying a hurt for years sooner than risk being seen to need help with it. You might be carrying other people's secrets as well, the friend who confided in you, the family matter no one mentions. You're good at holding them, and you've been doing it on your own for a long time.

In the body it's tension that sits deep, in the jaw or the lower back. At night it's sleep that turns over old wounds. In a close friendship it's doing the emotional heavy lifting for them while trusting nobody with yours. Tell one person you trust a single thing you'd normally guard, and see what they do with it.
moon.reversed:
Sealed up, the card on a Scorpio Moon buries the overwhelm so deep that even you lose track of it. It comes out sideways, as suspicion, brooding, or a sudden cold shoulder to someone who didn't see it coming. The card's fire simmering under your water builds a heat you keep clamped down, and the load gets heavier for being secret. Mars colours Saturn in your sign and keeps you braced for a fight.

It shows in sleep that churns and in grudges you feed quietly. It shows in a body holding stress like a fist. With a partner it might be jealousy that's really exhaustion. Let one thing out to one safe person before it festers, in a low-key way, on a walk or in the car.

rising.upright:
In a crisis, people tend to ring the Scorpio rising. You meet the world watchful and guarded, you give little away and read everything, and that controlled intensity makes people assume you can handle anything. So they bring you the heavy things, the emergency, the secret, the difficult conversation someone else ought to be having. This card is what that costs you.

Your rising sign sits next to Sagittarius on the wheel, a semi-sextile with little common ground, and fire on water makes steam, so the load you attract chafes against the way you'd want to meet things. Mars rules your chart, with Pluto as its modern co-ruler, and Saturn takes on that Martial colour here, all pressure and no ease. Behind the impenetrable front the pressure keeps building, and you let nobody see it. People with this Ascendant are often the first call when things go wrong and the last person anyone checks on afterwards.

With new people you become the confidant for their troubles while telling them nothing of yours. At work you're handed the sensitive, hard jobs because you look unflappable. In a new relationship you hold the depth of the bond yourself and don't let your partner carry any of your weight. Let one person see a crack on purpose, a bad day or a worry, and notice they treat you no worse for it.
rising.reversed:
Blocked, the guarded Scorpio front turns into a fortress you can't get out of either. You look so completely in control that nobody imagines you need anything, and the unflappable look keeps pulling the heaviest jobs onto you. Mars rules your chart and takes up a defensive position when it's tired, so the harder things get, the less anyone sees.

It shows as a loneliness that looks like strength from outside. At work you absorb the hard things silently and pay for it later, out of sight. With family it might be being the one everyone calls with bad news. On a date it can come across as cold when you're actually worn out. Admit to one person that you're stretched, plainly, and let them offer something.

sun.upright:
This is one of Sagittarius's own cards. The Ten of Wands belongs to the last ten degrees of your sign, the stretch Saturn rules, so if your birthday falls between about the twelfth and the twenty-first of December it's your decan card outright. Sagittarius is the sign that reaches, the bigger plan, the next country, the idea that could change everything, and those last ten degrees are where Saturn comes in and asks what all that reaching is going to cost to carry.

Fire meeting fire turns things up, the good and the too much. You say yes to the big plan with your whole chest, then to the other big plan, and Saturn, only a visitor in Sagittarius with no power of its own there, doesn't stop you. It just hands you the bill later. What you'll recognise is that you overcommitted out of real excitement. Every one of those staves was a good idea at the time. Together they've crowded out the freedom they were meant to give you. Temperance is your sign's Major, a card about mixing things slowly in the right amounts, and that's the skill this card is short of.

At work it's the ambitious project plus the three others you agreed to because they all sounded brilliant in the room. With money it's spending on the strength of an optimism that hasn't paid off yet. Your body pays in a worn, restless tiredness. Finish one thing all the way before you start anything new, including the boring last part.
sun.reversed:
Upside down, your own sign's card turns the Sagittarius appetite for more into a heap of grand starts you can't keep up. You chased every exciting horizon and they're all half-built and all asking for something. Saturn bears down hardest on this part of your sign, and the freedom you spent so freely has gone sour into obligation. Fire on fire keeps you saying yes even while you sink.

It shows as big promises you can't keep and a reputation that runs ahead of what you deliver. With friends it's the trip you organised and then couldn't afford to go on. You'd sooner start something new than sit with the unfinished. Do the dull last tenth of one thing you began, and tell someone when it's done.

moon.upright:
A Sagittarius Moon needs room. An open diary, a door you could walk out of, the sense that if things get heavy you can always go somewhere new. That's why this is a hard card to draw for your tides. It's one of your own sign's cards, from the last ten degrees of Sagittarius, the stretch where Saturn settles in and pins things down. The freedom you rely on to feel alright has been fenced in by commitments, and you chose every one of them.

Fire on fire runs hot, so your restlessness and your yeses both come big. Saturn has no power in Sagittarius and takes on the colour of Jupiter, your Moon's ruler, which makes it expansive even as it weighs you down, so the load keeps growing. You'll know a feeling of being trapped that doesn't quite make sense, since nobody forced any of it on you. Part of the weight is the tasks. More of it is losing the escape hatch, the sense that you could just go if you needed to.

It shows as a low sort of claustrophobia, snappiness when a plan gets pinned down, and restless sleep. With a partner it can be wanting to leave the room during a conversation about next year. Your body might want a long walk more than anything. Keep one day completely empty, and guard it from everyone, yourself included.
moon.reversed:
Fenced in, a Sagittarius Moon under the reversed Ten gets jumpy and trapped. You took on too much, lost the open horizon, and the part of you that copes by knowing it can leave is quietly panicking. With Saturn pinning down your own sign's card, the claustrophobia has nowhere to go.

It shows as irritability whenever plans close in, and a pull to bolt from things you agreed to. Sleep goes patchy. You might snap at anyone who adds to the load, or book a trip you can't really afford just to feel a door open. Jupiter rules your Moon and needs something to look forward to. Keep an evening free of any plan, go for a walk with no destination, and don't check your phone until you're home.

rising.upright:
Sagittarius rising comes in open and friendly, up for anything and honest to a fault, and people read you as someone who'll say yes. So they ask. You start things with a big optimistic yes and a real appetite for them, and that eagerness looks like endless capacity, so the commitments pile up faster than you notice. This card is the result.

It's one of your own sign's cards, from its last ten degrees, so it's personal. Look at the man in the picture. He's so bent over the bundle that he can't see the road, which is an odd position for a sign that's all about the view. Fire on fire turns up your enthusiasm, and Saturn, a guest with no power in Sagittarius, mostly turns up once the commitments fall due. Jupiter rules your chart, and Jupiter makes everything bigger, including the number of things you've said you'll do. You seem free and easy, and under all you've agreed to, you feel boxed in.

In a new crowd you're quickly the fun one who's suddenly overbooked. Meeting strangers, you promise adventures and favours on a wave of good feeling. At work it's volunteering for the offsite, the new project and the charity run in the same week. Before your next enthusiastic yes, check the diary, and let one good offer go by.
rising.reversed:
With the card reversed, Sagittarius rising's easy openness becomes a yes you can't rein in. You keep agreeing because saying no feels like shutting a door on something good, and your up-for-anything reputation keeps the invitations and obligations coming. Jupiter rules your chart and likes more of everything. Fire on fire gives the enthusiasm no off switch.

It costs you a life so booked up that the freedom you love has gone, with a vague dread under the cheerful surface. People see the fun one and never the stretched one. At work it's deadlines you're late on because you took on too much. Let a good opportunity pass on purpose, say a plain no, and see what you do with the space.

sun.upright:
Saturn rules Capricorn, and Saturn is the planet behind this card, so it comes to a Capricorn Sun with real authority. You're built to carry, to take responsibility and to climb by sheer staying power, and this card shows what happens when that real strength turns into a load with no ceiling.

Saturn is at home in Capricorn, strong and unforced, which means the discipline in you is genuine. So is the danger, because you'll shoulder more and more and call it duty long after it stopped doing anyone any good. Sagittarius sits just behind Capricorn on the wheel, a neighbouring sign with little in common, and your earth has no natural sympathy with the card's fire, so its restless reaching never quite feels like yours. You carry it anyway. The Devil, Capricorn's own Major, is about chains people could take off and don't. I've seen this with a lot of Capricorn Suns. Your sense of worth is tangled up with how much you can bear, so putting anything down feels like failing.

At work it's taking on the whole mountain and not complaining. In your family it's being the provider who won't be seen to struggle. The body wears it in the knees, the back and the joints. At the end of the next working day, count what you deliberately didn't do, and let that count as a good day.
sun.reversed:
Upturned on a Capricorn Sun, the Ten becomes a compulsion to carry. Stopping feels like failing, so you don't stop. With Saturn at home in your sign, the discipline that should serve you just keeps adding duty with no upper limit, and the climb has lost its top.

It shows as overwork worn like a badge, and a body starting to protest in the joints and back. It shows as a coldness toward people who seem to carry less than you. You measure everyone by output, yourself most of all. With family it's missing things and telling yourself they understand. Choose one limit, a finishing time or a day off, and keep it the way you'd keep a promise to a client.

moon.upright:
A Capricorn Moon feels safest when it's in control and doesn't have to lean on anyone. You look after yourself. You'd put up with being exhausted before you'd let yourself be a burden. With this card on your Moon, that self-reliance has become a weight you won't share, and I'd guess nobody around you knows how heavy it's got.

Saturn rules Capricorn and is the planet on this card, so this goes straight to how you're made, the part of you that soothes itself by taking on more and asking for nothing. With Saturn at home here the discipline is solid, and so is the loneliness that comes with it. Sagittarius, next door to your Moon's sign and sharing little with it, adds a restless extra load, and since fire and earth don't naturally connect, that load never quite warms you. It's worth knowing that Saturn's own Major is The World, a card of something finished and complete. The planet that rules your Moon's sign likes things to end as much as it likes them carried. Needing help still feels like weakness to you, so you carry your feelings as well as your jobs, privately, and call it being strong.

It shows in a body that holds stress in the jaw and shoulders. It shows as telling a partner you're fine when you aren't. And there's a quiet belief that rest has to be earned. Let one person carry one thing for you this week, and put up with how uncomfortable it feels.
moon.reversed:
The card reversed on a Capricorn Moon hardens self-reliance into refusing to need anyone at all. You carry everything alone, tell no one you're struggling, and then quietly resent that nobody helps, though you've made helping nearly impossible. With Saturn at home in your sign, the discipline and the isolation both run deep.

It shows as a flat, joyless kind of getting on with it, a body stiff with held stress, and a sense that showing need would make you a burden. You might feel most alone exactly when you're coping best. With a parent it can be the old role of the child who never caused any trouble. Tell one safe person one true thing about how you are, and let them answer however they like.

rising.upright:
People trust a Capricorn rising with responsibility almost on sight. You come across as serious and capable, someone who plainly knows how to get things done, and that's how this card loads your Ascendant. Looking that solid is a standing invitation to hand you more. Saturn, the card's own planet, rules your rising sign, so the whole theme of duty and weight is written into how you come across.

Sagittarius sits just before Capricorn, a neighbour with little shared ground, and the card's fire sits on your earth without any warmth between them, so the loads you attract always fit a bit badly, even as you accept them. Capricorn rising often looks older than it is when young, and people go on treating you as the grown-up in the room. What they don't see is what it costs to keep that up, and you probably don't mention it, because mentioning it would spoil the front. Capricorn risings often get made a manager within a year of starting somewhere and never quite get to be junior.

With a new employer you're the safe pair of hands, and then the overloaded one. Strangers read you as older and steadier than you feel. In your family you're the one everyone assumes can handle the crisis. In the next meeting where it matters, let your capable surface show one honest limit, out loud.
rising.reversed:
Blocked, the capable Capricorn front turns into a cage of competence. You look so on top of things that nobody dreams of offering help, and the dependable look keeps drawing the heaviest jobs toward you. Saturn rules your rising sign, so the whole machinery of duty is built into how you meet the world, and it keeps running when you're empty.

At work it shows as being the backstop everyone assumes is fine. With friends it's being admired for coping and privately worn thin. With family it's the one who drives everyone to the airport and never gets a lift. On a date it can look like reserve when it's tiredness. Say out loud to one person that you're at your limit, and ask them to take one specific thing.

sun.upright:
Causes, committees, the fundraiser, a friend's start-up that needs a hand. An Aquarius Sun collects them, because you want to be useful to something bigger than yourself and to stay independent while you do it, and the Ten of Wands says the commitments have piled up on top of the person. Saturn is the traditional ruler of Aquarius, so this card's planet is on home ground with you. Its themes of structure and duty are part of how you're made, for good and for overload.

Sagittarius sits sextile to Aquarius, two signs apart, a friendly opening, and air and fire are natural allies, so you say yes to every worthy project easily. The pile grows out of good intentions. You take on the community's weight because someone has to and you can see how it ought to be done. The Star is your sign's Major, a woman pouring water out freely, and I think that's how you see yourself, the one who gives. What this card shows is you organising, fixing and carrying for the collective while running on empty in private, because your principles won't let you say the group can manage without you.

At work it's being the person who holds the systems together and never gets thanked. In your friendships it's being the organiser everyone relies on. With a cause or a committee, it's the meetings you chair and the emails you write at eleven at night. Let a group you care about solve one problem without you, and stay out of it even if they solve it badly.
sun.reversed:
Overloaded, an Aquarius Sun won't let the group manage without it. You carry the collective's weight on principle, and with Saturn at home in your sign the sense of duty runs deep and is hard to switch off. The ideals that give you meaning keep signing you up for more than one person can hold, and air keeps feeding the card's fire with every new yes.

It shows as burnout in the service of something worthwhile, and a resentment you feel guilty for having. You'll help a stranger's cause while ignoring how tired you are. At work it might be the project nobody else understands, so nobody else can take it off you. Step back from one commitment, tell the group in a short message, and let them rise to it.

moon.upright:
An Aquarius Moon likes a bit of distance from its feelings. You're happier being a good friend to many than being pinned into one person's intense need, and you handle upsets by thinking them through, often on your own. This card suggests the duties you've taken on for other people have crowded out the space you need.

Saturn rules Aquarius in the traditional scheme, so this is close to home. It's the part of you that copes by staying useful and a little detached, and never quite gets round to feeling things through. The sextile to Sagittarius and the friendliness between fire and air mean you agree to help readily, from the head, and the load builds while your own feelings wait politely to one side. You handle everyone's practical needs and neglect your own moods, because tending to them is the thing you're least at ease with. There's a loneliness in it, a strange one, since you're surrounded by people you're helping.

It shows as a calendar full of obligations to others, and in sleep that doesn't quite restore you. With a close friend it might be listening to their problems for hours and changing the subject when they ask about yours. Let yourself feel one thing properly, without solving it, and drop one duty to the group so there's time to.
moon.reversed:
Pushed too far, an Aquarius Moon copes by floating above the whole thing. You go on handling everyone's logistics while feeling less and less, cool and useful on top with the strain building underneath. Saturn, the old ruler of your Moon's sign, reinforces the habit of managing feelings instead of having them. The load is real even if you've gone numb to it.

It shows as a packed schedule and a distance from your own body and moods. You might feel lonely in a way you can't place. At home it can look like being pleasant and far away. Name one feeling plainly to one person, in a sentence, out loud, and cancel one duty so there's room to sit with it.

rising.upright:
Somebody has to run the residents' group, and it's usually the Aquarius rising. You come across as friendly and a little detached, original, fair-minded, someone who treats everyone the same, and people trust you to be even-handed, so they hand you the coordinating and the fixing. You meet the world through ideas and a certain cool independence, and looking unbothered and capable draws responsibility your way.

Saturn is the traditional ruler of your rising sign, so duty and structure are built into your approach. Sagittarius sits sextile to Aquarius, a cooperative angle, and the two elements get on, so you take on the group's tasks readily and the load mounts. You look independent, and you've agreed to hold far more for other people than anyone guesses. I've seen a lot of Aquarius risings end up running the club, the book group, the fantasy football league, because they were the one person in the room who seemed calm enough to do it.

With new people you're the fair organiser straight away, and the overburdened one soon after. At work you end up owning the systems nobody else wants to maintain. With a new friend it's being the one who remembers everyone's dietary requirements for the barbecue. The next time you're asked, admit one real limit, and let the group carry itself.
rising.reversed:
This card upside down on Aquarius rising turns the cool front into a hiding place. You look independent and unbothered, so nobody imagines you need relief, and the capable look keeps the group's tasks flowing your way. Saturn rules your rising sign, and duty is built into the mask. Fire and air make agreeing very easy for you.

What it costs is holding things together for everyone while feeling oddly unseen. At work you're the systems person nobody thinks to check on. In a group of friends it's organising everything and then feeling like an outsider at the event. On a date it can come across as distant when you're just tired. Say plainly that you're overstretched, and let the group take up the slack.

sun.upright:
Pisces Suns lead with compassion. You feel what's going on in a room before anyone speaks, and your boundaries are soft enough that other people's troubles wash straight in. So this card, drawn for what you're building, is mostly about how much of what you carry was never yours in the first place.

Sagittarius squares Pisces, both mutable signs, three apart, and a square is friction that forces action. The card's restless, take-on-more energy keeps colliding with your softer nature and turning into obligations. Your water and the card's fire are opposed elements, and you'll feel that as a rasp against your gentleness. Saturn has no standing in Pisces and takes on Jupiter's colour, so it swells whatever it touches. Your sign does hold one piece of Saturn, though. Saturn rules the first ten degrees of Pisces, the Eight of Cups, the card of someone walking away from a row of cups they've carefully stacked. That's Saturn's gift to your sign, the ability to leave, and it's exactly what this card needs from you. You probably find it the hardest thing in the world.

At work it's the emotional labour nobody names, calming people down, noticing who's upset. With friends you're the one everyone rings in a crisis. Your body registers it as a foggy, drained heaviness. Pick one burden that belongs to someone else and hand it back, kindly and completely.
sun.reversed:
With the Ten upside down, a Pisces Sun can absorb so much of everyone else that there's hardly any of you left. You take on every burden offered because refusing feels cruel, and Saturn has no grip in your sign to give you the edge that would help. The card's fire and your water make a steam that leaves you foggy and worn out.

It shows as a longing to escape, into sleep, screens or a glass of wine, and a resentment you feel too guilty to name. At work you've become the place everyone offloads. The Eight of Cups is in your sign for a reason, and walking away from one thing would help. Draw one line, hand back one thing that was never yours, and put up with the guilt that follows until it passes.

moon.upright:
Some of what you're feeling isn't yours. A Pisces Moon feels the whole room and can't always tell which feelings belong to whom. You need quiet and time alone to recover, and you soothe yourself by drifting somewhere softer, a book, music, a long bath, sleep. So the weight in this card, for you, is mostly other people's emotions, soaked up without you meaning to.

Saturn has no footing in Pisces, so it presses on you without helping. The card's fire against your water wears you thin. The square between Sagittarius and Pisces keeps stirring up more to feel and more to fix. Jupiter rules your Moon, and Jupiter makes things bigger, including the feelings you've taken in. The Moon, which is your sign's Major, is a card of things half seen at night, and this load is hard to see the edges of in the same way. You'll know the pattern of picking up someone else's pain as if it were yours and then not being able to put it down, because you never noticed picking it up.

It shows as a bone-deep tiredness after time with people, even people you love, and a pull to escape into sleep or a screen. You might carry a mood for a whole day before realising it started with a friend's phone call. Spend some proper time alone after seeing people, and let one person's trouble stay theirs.
moon.reversed:
Flooded, a Pisces Moon under the reversed card loses the last of its boundaries. You've soaked up everyone's pain until you can't tell it from your own, and Saturn, powerless in your sign, offers nothing to hold you together. The fire and water in this pairing leave you frayed and foggy, and you might want nothing more than to disappear for a while.

It shows as escapism, a heaviness sleep doesn't cure, and a weepy, porous overwhelm you can't explain. You may be carrying moods that started in other people. Try something physical and grounding first, cold water on your face, bare feet on the floor, and then one clear sentence to the person whose feelings you've taken on, so they can have them back.

rising.upright:
Strangers tell a Pisces rising their life story on the train. You're receptive and hard to pin down, you seem to take on the colour of whatever's around you, and that gentle openness makes people feel they can bring you anything. So they bring you their troubles and their jobs, and you take them, and that's the load in this card. You approach life without hard edges, and looking so receptive is an invitation for others to unload.

Your rising sign squares the card's Sagittarius, three mutable signs apart, and fire on water makes steam, so what you attract chafes against your soft way of meeting things. Jupiter rules your chart, with Neptune as its modern co-ruler, and Saturn has no standing here, so the edges you most need are the hardest for you to hold. You seem open and undefended, and you've quietly taken on a lot because you couldn't find the place to refuse. Pisces rising gets asked for help by people it's known for ten minutes, and usually says yes.

Within a day of meeting someone, you're their confidant and their helper. At work you pick up the tension in every meeting and carry it home. On a date you might spend the evening looking after the other person's nerves. Meet the next request with a soft, clear no, and notice that you're still kind afterwards.
rising.reversed:
The reversed card on Pisces rising turns the soft front into something you hide behind. You're so open that everyone offloads onto you, and nobody thinks to ask if you're alright. Saturn, with no standing in your sign, keeps the weight coming and doesn't give you the edges to stop it. The square with Sagittarius keeps the demands arriving.

What you lose is a sense of where you end and other people begin, and there's a quiet exhaustion under all that gentleness. Fire and water make steam, and here it comes out as tears at odd moments. At work it's absorbing every tension and taking it home. With friends it's agreeing to everything and then going missing for a week. Practise one clear, kind refusal and let it stand, even while it feels awful.

1.upright:
Look at how the man in this card is walking. He's bent almost double, arms wrapped round ten staves held out in front of him, and he can't see the road for them. In the first house, that's your body and your bearing. This is the house of how you walk into a room and how you start things, an angular house, one of the corners of the chart that everyone can see. Drawn here, the card suggests you've been starting each day already loaded.

The astrology pulls two ways. The card's Sagittarius makes an easy trine with Aries, the first house's natural sign, both fire, so taking things on comes with no friction and the pile grows smoothly. Same element, so everything's louder. But the card runs on Saturn, and Saturn is in fall in Aries, badly placed against everything this house wants, which is to move freely and begin. So the urge to just get going keeps getting dragged back by weight it can't shake off. You'll know the feeling. You brace before you move. You carry tension in the way you stand, and people who meet you can see you're capable and can also see you're carrying something.

It lives in shoulders and an upper back that ache for no clear reason, and in a walk that's gone heavy. It shows in how you throw yourself at each new start until there's nothing left for the middle. At the beginning of a job it's taking on everything in the first week. Begin one thing empty-handed, without promising anything, and see how it goes.
1.reversed:
When this card turns over in the first house, the body usually starts forcing the issue. You've begun too many things braced and strained, and with Saturn in fall in the house's natural sign, pushing harder only runs the tank drier. Fire on fire with nowhere to go ends up as burnout. Your face may be showing the strain before you've admitted it.

It shows in how you carry yourself, a hunch, a clenched jaw, a tiredness that's there before you're properly awake. People have started asking if you're alright. Mars is this house's natural ruler and it doesn't like being told to stop. Start fewer things, and the first time your body sets a limit, a headache or a sore back, listen to it and rest.

2.upright:
Money and self-worth share the second house, and with the Ten of Wands here they've got tangled together. This is the house of what you earn, what you own and what you think you're worth, a succedent house where things are built up and kept. Drawn into it, the card ties your sense of your own value to how much you can carry.

The card's Sagittarius sits at a quincunx to Taurus, the second house's natural sign, five signs apart with nothing in common. So there's a constant mismatch between the restless drive to earn more and take on more, and the steady Taurus wish to simply have enough and enjoy it. Fire and earth are neutral here, so effort and reward have to be introduced to each other every time, and they don't always get on. Saturn brings the grind of proving your worth through sheer output. You take the extra shift, the second job, the weekend freelancing, and the security you're chasing moves a bit further off each time.

It shows in a bank balance built on overwork, with not much time left to enjoy what it buys. It shows in possessions that take more looking after than you meant, the second car, the storage unit, the big garden. Your self-worth may dip the moment you stop producing. Work out on paper what you'd need to earn to have enough, and let that be the number you aim for.
2.reversed:
Turned over in the second house, this card can make stopping feel like losing value. You keep earning and buying and over-committing your time and money to feel secure, and because the card's Sagittarius sits at an awkward quincunx to this house's Taurus, the effort never settles into the calm you're after. Saturn keeps the account of proving yourself open.

It shows as money made at the cost of everything else, a budget of time and energy stretched thin, and a nagging feeling that you'd be worth nothing if you slowed down. Venus is this house's natural ruler and it needs some pleasure in the money. Keep one thing that doesn't have to be earned, an afternoon, a treat, a day of leave you actually take, and don't justify it to anyone.

3.upright:
Everyday talk lives in the third house. Messages, calls, siblings and neighbours, the short trips across town, the things you're learning, the general business of staying in touch. It's a cadent house, the kind that takes things in and passes them along, and with the Ten of Wands here, your voice and your daily mind are carrying too much.

Sagittarius, the card's sign, is directly opposite Gemini, this house's natural sign, the far end of the same line.
